response.sql: WITH lab_pt AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(CASE WHEN l.ALB IS NOT NULL AND l.TP IS NOT NULL THEN l.ALB - l.TP END) AS alb_tp, AVG(CASE WHEN l.APTT IS NOT NULL AND l.PT IS NOT NULL THEN l.APTT - l.PT END) AS aptt_pt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sex_avg AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb_tp) AS alb_tp, AVG(aptt_pt) AS aptt_pt FROM lab_pt GROUP BY SEX), threshold AS (SELECT AVG(aptt_pt) AS mean_aptt_pt FROM sex_avg), kept AS (SELECT s.* FROM sex_avg s, threshold t WHERE s.aptt_pt > t.mean_aptt_pt) SELECT AVG(alb_tp) AS alb_tp_figure, AVG(aptt_pt) AS aptt_pt_figure, AVG(aptt_pt) - (SELECT mean_aptt_pt FROM threshold) AS aptt_pt_excess FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: Each lab record is one test: ALB − TP and APTT − PT are computed per record only where both values in the pair are non-null, then averaged per patient (patients with no valid pair get a NULL figure and are ignored by later averages).
Each sex-level average is an unweighted mean of patient figures, and the threshold is the unweighted mean of the sex-level APTT − PT averages (not weighted by patient count).
Patient.SEX values are grouped as-is, so NULL and blank strings form separate groups, each treated as its own sex group as the request specifies.
The final row's ALB − TP and APTT − PT figures are unweighted averages across the kept sex-level averages, and the excess is that APTT − PT figure minus the threshold mean.
